content.en: Cropping systems and terminologies form the foundation of agricultural economics within the **Indian Economy**. In the context of **UPSC GS-3**, evaluating how land is utilized across different seasons dictates national food security, cropping intensity, and sustainable resource allocation. Policy documents like the **Economic Survey** and recommendations from **NITI Aayog** frequently emphasize diversifying cropping patterns to mitigate climate risks and enhance farmer incomes.

rows.en: Growing only one crop species on the same land year after year, which can deplete specific soil nutrients.
rows.hi: Growing only one crop species on the same land year after year, which can deplete specific soil nutrients.

rows.en: Growing two or more crops simultaneously on the same field in a definite row pattern to maximize resource use.
rows.hi: Growing two or more crops simultaneously on the same field in a definite row pattern to maximize resource use.

rows.en: Planting a succeeding crop before the harvesting of the preceding crop, ensuring continuous land occupation.
rows.hi: Planting a succeeding crop before the harvesting of the preceding crop, ensuring continuous land occupation.

rows.en: Growing different types of crops in sequential succession on the same plot to improve soil health and break pest cycles.
rows.hi: Growing different types of crops in sequential succession on the same plot to improve soil health and break pest cycles.

definition.en: The number of crops raised on the same field during an agricultural year, expressed as a percentage of the total net sown area.
definition.hi: The number of crops raised on the same field during an agricultural year, expressed as a percentage of the total net sown area.

definition.en: The practice of growing two or more crops on the same piece of land during one calendar year, heavily supported by irrigation infrastructure.
definition.hi: The practice of growing two or more crops on the same piece of land during one calendar year, heavily supported by irrigation infrastructure.

content.en: Growing two or more crops simultaneously without any distinct row arrangement, serving as an insurance against crop failure due to erratic rainfall.
content.hi: Growing two or more crops simultaneously without any distinct row arrangement, serving as an insurance against crop failure due to erratic rainfall.

content.en: A method of harvesting a crop by leaving the roots and lower parts of the plant intact to allow a stubble crop to grow.
content.hi: A method of harvesting a crop by leaving the roots and lower parts of the plant intact to allow a stubble crop to grow.

content.en: Students often confuse 'intercropping' (growing crops in definite rows simultaneously) with 'mixed cropping' (growing mixed seeds without rows). Both have distinct economic and agronomic implications.
